# `silk/json/reflect`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Write a struct as a JSON object from its fields, and read one back, without writing each field
by hand.

## When to use
Use [`JsonReflect.write`](#JsonReflect.impl.write) for a struct whose fields each implement `Serialize`, and
[`JsonReflect.read`](#JsonReflect.impl.read) for a struct whose fields each implement `Deserialize`. Call them
directly, or from the `Serialize` and `Deserialize` implementations of the struct.

## Details
The fields are written in declaration order. Only the fields that this module can see are
written, so the private fields of a type from another module are left out. Writing does not
allocate.

Reading finds each field's member by its key, in any order, and builds the struct with one
field initializer per field. Members that name no field are skipped.

## Errors
- `JsonError` from a field value, or `MissingField` when the object has no member for a field.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.

## Gotchas
[`JsonReflect.read`](#JsonReflect.impl.read) needs every field of the struct to be public, since it initializes each
one. It scans the object once for each field, so prefer a hand-written `Deserialize` for an
object with many members.

Import as `JsonReflect` with `import silk.json.reflect { JsonReflect }`.

Public declarations: 1.

## `JsonReflect`

```silk
pub struct JsonReflect
```

The owner type of the reflection writer. It has no fields and is never constructed.

```silk
impl JsonReflect
```

<a id="JsonReflect.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write<T>(value: &T, options: &JsonOptions)
    -> () ! JsonError | WriterError ? &mut Writer
```

Writes `value` as a JSON object with one member for each field that is visible here, in
declaration order.

#### Details

Each field must implement `Serialize`. A type that is not a struct with named fields, or a
field without `Serialize`, is a compile error.

#### Errors

- `JsonError` from a field value.
- `WriterError` if the `Writer` fails. Bytes that it accepted before the failure stay written.
  The object can be incomplete.

<a id="JsonReflect.impl.read"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub effect fn read<T>(scanner: &mut JsonScanner<'_>)
    -> T ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads a JSON object from `scanner` as a `T`, one field for each member whose key is the
field's name. It leaves the next token unread.

#### Details

Each field must be public and implement `Deserialize`. Members may come in any order, and a
member whose key names no field is skipped. When a key appears twice, the first member wins.

#### Errors

- `JsonError` with reason `TypeMismatch` if the value is not an object, `MissingField` if
  the object has no member for a field, or the error of a member value.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply a field value.

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.json.reflect { JsonReflect }
import silk.json.scanner { JsonError, JsonScanner }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

struct Point {
  pub x: i32,
  pub y: i32,
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! JsonError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut scanner = JsonScanner.make(b"{\"y\": 4, \"x\": 3}")
  let point = run JsonReflect.read<Point>(&mut scanner) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return point.x * 10 + point.y
}
```
